items.title: Recruiter demand is at a record high
items.sponsor_flag: Juicebox sponsor block (vendor claims: 800M+ profiles, 3x replies); flagged and not used as evidence. Event plugs for PromptMates' own live shows.
items.reader_fit: Strong for UK readers on the pay-in-ads pledge and Indeed figure; the recruiter-demand stat is US tech only; agent-manager idea is opinion from OpenAI's CPO.

points.claim: Open tech recruiter jobs are at a record high while US engineering hires are below half the 2022 peak
points.figure: 2,857 open tech recruiter jobs this month, up 323% from a low of 676; about 113,000 US engineering hires in the year to April 2026
points.quote: TrueUp counts 2,857 open tech recruiter jobs this month, up 323% from a low of 676, and Lenny Rachitsky calls that a record high. US engineering hires in the year to April 2026 were about 113,000, less than half the 2022 peak, so the work per hire has grown.
points.market: US (tech); recruiter job count market unstated, likely US-weighted

points.claim: UK government has committed to a pay-in-job-ads law, not yet law; UK pay disclosure in postings has fallen
points.figure: 58% of UK postings included pay in the three months to June, down from 64% in September 2024
points.quote: The UK government has committed to a law requiring salaries in job adverts, but it isn't law yet, and is asking employers to publish pay now.

points.claim: Fake employer AccuraSoftHire used ID-verified LinkedIn recruiter profiles and a malicious npm package in its take-home test
points.figure: AccuraSoftHire; LinkedIn verification shield; malicious npm package
points.quote: The shield only confirms a government ID, not the job title or the company

points.claim: Remote's People team replaced seven HR software contracts with tools built with Claude, including an in-house ATS
points.figure: seven HR contracts not renewed; six people incl. three recruiters; ATS shipped in five months; more than 24,000 applications
points.quote: Six people, including three recruiters, shipped an ATS in five months that has handled more than 24,000 applications, without saying how screening works or what it costs.

points.claim: OpenAI's CPO expects recruiters to become recruiting agent managers and would drop junior/senior labels
points.figure: Arvind KC, Chief People Officer at OpenAI; Theory Ventures Office Hours with Tomasz Tunguz
points.quote: A salesperson becomes a sales agent manager and a recruiter becomes a recruiting agent manager, with scope and pay following how well someone coordinates a few humans and many virtual coworkers towards an outcome.
points.attributed_to: Arvind KC, as summarised by Theory Ventures

points.claim: Claude Meetings beta joins Google Meet calls but stays out of calls with outside guests by default
points.figure: Claude Meetings, beta, Team and Enterprise plans, Google Meet only
points.quote: By default it stays out of calls with outside guests, so it won't join candidate interviews unless an admin allows it.

items.title: The fake recruiter behind a $6.3bn hack
items.sponsor_flag: Scede sponsor block (Claude Skills webinar, 17 Nov); flagged. LinkedIn's 83% fewer profiles is a vendor claim.
items.reader_fit: High: the Employ AI-time stat is quotable, the Arsentev agent case gives real numbers plus a UK GDPR/EU AI Act note, and the Binance story affects every in-house team.

points.claim: Binance's record theft began with a fake recruitment process and a malware 'assignment'
points.figure: $6.3bn (BBC figure); October 2026; FBI attributes to North Korea
points.quote: An engineer was approached on a legitimate job platform, sat a video interview with a fake HR representative and a second round with a fake "CEO", then was told to download an "assignment" that installed malware on his work laptop.
points.attributed_to: BBC (figure), Binance's own report, Chainalysis breakdown

points.claim: Recruiters have adopted AI but fewer are getting time back; candidate fraud up
points.figure: 68% of teams use AI; 18% shifted more than half their time to higher-value work, down from 26% in 2025; confirmed candidate fraud 27% (from 23%); 29% cite scheduling delays; survey of 1,200+
points.quote: Employ's 2026 Recruiter Nation survey of more than 1,200 HR and recruiting professionals finds 68% of teams use AI, yet only 18% of recruiters using it have shifted more than half their time to higher-value work, down from 26% in 2025.
points.attributed_to: Employ Recruiter Nation 2026, via Lever blog

points.claim: A Claude agent ran the front of one company's hiring funnel; no-shows were the bottleneck
points.figure: 36 days; 1,973 applications read; 138 interviews booked; 37 no-shows; 68.6% attended; 2 of 7 HIRE-rated still working at day 36 vs 6 of 12 MAYBE
points.quote: 37 booked interviews ended in a no-show, as many as failed the supervisor's interview (also 37). Only 68.6% of bookings were attended, so 31% didn't turn up.
points.market: US (US-facing telemedicine company); one company, no control group

points.claim: The agent case raised compliance gaps: rejections nobody read and no disclosure of AI
points.figure: 3 NO-rated candidates rejected; 2 had passed a human interview; UK GDPR; EU AI Act high-risk
points.quote: Candidates were not told that the video interviewer was an AI avatar or that a model scored them, and were not offered a human route.
points.market: US case; UK and EU rules noted by the newsletter

points.claim: LinkedIn Hiring Assistant 2 adds memory of how each recruiter hires
points.figure: Hiring Assistant 2; English-language customers; 83% fewer profiles reviewed (vendor claim)
points.quote: LinkedIn says users review 83% fewer profiles.

points.claim: Claudia Sahm argues a task audit misses why juniors are hired
points.figure: Jason Furman (former CEA chair); Claudia Sahm; $2,400 a year AI budget
points.quote: A task list tells you what a person does on a given day," Sahm writes. "It does not tell you why the organization hired them.

items.title: How Do Candidates Know Your Recruiters Are Real?
items.sponsor_flag: Metaview (fillmore sourcing agent) sponsor block; flagged.
items.reader_fit: Practical for UK in-house TA: five principles a team can act on this week; no data. Overlaps heavily with DDR85 and draws on it.

points.claim: Impersonators reuse a genuine recruiter's identity while changing the contact address, so profiles are not proof
points.figure: Stacy Zapar; Tenfold 'Might Be Fake' resource; 'Fake Stacy'
points.quote: impostors can reuse a genuine recruiter’s name, branding and LinkedIn details while changing the actual contact address. That’s why a polished signature or convincing profile isn’t reliable proof.

points.claim: Employers should offer a verified candidate portal and published channels
points.figure: No figure
points.quote: Email should notify. The verified portal should confirm.

points.claim: Tell candidates what you will never ask
points.figure: No figure
points.quote: candidates should be cautious about requests to install unfamiliar software, run code or provide banking information outside an appropriate, verified process.
points.attributed_to: Darren Bush, building on Luke Eaton's recommendations

points.claim: Staff need a confidential route to report suspicious external job approaches
points.figure: Matt Buckland observation
points.quote: An employer should make clear that staff can seek confidential security advice about suspicious external job approaches without disclosing their career intentions to their manager.

points.claim: Design recruitment safety jointly across TA, HR and Cybersecurity
points.figure: No figure
points.quote: Trust shouldn’t be an extra step. It should be designed into hiring.

items.title: We’re so focused on fake candidates, we’re missing the fake recruiters
items.reader_fit: Useful framing piece for TA leaders: recruitment fraud as a company security risk; Binance timeline is the most detailed of the week; few actionables (those come in the 13 Nov follow-up).

points.claim: Recruitment fraud has a third victim: the jobseeker's current employer
points.figure: No figure
points.quote: The job seeker may already be someone else’s employee. An attack on an individual can also become an attack route into their current employer.

points.claim: Binance's reported loss and recovery figures
points.figure: $6.34bn affected; approximately $2.85bn frozen or intercepted by 3 November; 29 October; 20 October
points.quote: Binance reported $6.34bn in affected digital assets, with approximately $2.85bn frozen or intercepted by 3 November.
points.attributed_to: Binance's own account, as relayed by Darren Bush

points.claim: The fake interview was one stage of a months-long attack, not the sole cause
points.figure: June to October 2026
points.quote: One crucial detail: the fake interview was part of a months-long, multi-stage attack, not the sole cause.

points.claim: Reporting culture must not require staff to disclose a private job search
points.figure: Matt Buckland observation
points.quote: We can’t build a reporting culture that requires people to disclose their career intentions.

points.claim: Companies should warn staff about interview software, links and coding assignments
points.figure: No figure
points.quote: They should warn employees about unfamiliar interview software, unexpected links, executable files and coding assignments, and make it clear that security teams want early reports — including when someone has already clicked.

items.title: Issue 85 - The Hiring Safety Playbook
items.sponsor_flag: No real sponsor: the 'sponsor' block is satire attributed to Kim Jong Un. Ignore it.
items.reader_fit: Highest of the week for UK and US in-house TA: a complete, copy-ready playbook with templates and UK (Action Fraud) and US (IC3) reporting routes; some IT steps need handing to security.

points.claim: One fake-interview group infected over 30,000 devices in eight months
points.figure: 30,000+ devices in 100+ countries; eight months; joint advisory dated 18 Sept 2026
points.quote: **30,000+** devices infected in 100+ countries by one fake-interview group in eight months (joint advisory, 18 Sept 2026)
points.attributed_to: A joint advisory of 18 Sept 2026 (issuing agencies not named in the email)

points.claim: Smaller fake-interview attacks cost millions before Binance
points.figure: $14.3m; 18 months
points.quote: **$14.3m** lost to dozens of smaller fake-interview attacks in the 18 months before Binance (Chainalysis)

points.claim: Binance says it stopped dozens of North Korea-linked attempts this year
points.figure: 57 attempts in 2026
points.quote: **57** North Korea-linked attempts Binance says it detected and stopped in 2026, including fake interviews

points.claim: Eight-step candidate trust stack a small TA team can do in a week
points.figure: Eight steps; SPF, DKIM and DMARC
points.quote: Eight steps. A small TA team can get through all of them in a week.

points.claim: Stop running take-homes as local repos or zips
points.figure: No figure
points.quote: No take-homes as zip files or repos that candidates must run locally. Use a hosted environment, a live session or a read-only review.

points.claim: No company device, no system access for new hires
points.figure: No figure
points.quote: No company device, no system access. Kit lands before day one, or day one moves.
points.market: unstated; UK reporting route Action Fraud (0300 123 2040), US FBI IC3
